title: The Bamboo Broken by the Wind
translation: O mathematician, a bamboo standing on level ground, 32 hastas tall, was broken at one point by the force of the wind. Its top touched the ground 16 hastas from its base. Tell me, friend, at how many hastas from the root was it broken?
translation_hi: हे गणितज्ञ, समतल भूमि पर खड़ा 32 हाथ ऊँचा एक बाँस हवा के वेग से एक स्थान पर टूट गया। हे मित्र, उसका सिरा जड़ से 16 हाथ की दूरी पर भूमि को छू गया। बताओ, वह जड़ से कितने हाथ ऊपर टूटा?

words.meaning: from the force of the wind

question: At how many hastas from the root did the bamboo break?
solution:
Let the break be x hastas up. The broken part (32 − x) becomes the hypotenuse:

x² + 16² = (32 − x)²  ⟹  256 = 1024 − 64x  ⟹  x = 12 hastas

Bhaskara's rule: x = ½ (h − b²/h) = ½ (32 − 256/32) = ½ (24) = 12

Science link: this is exactly the same rule as the peacock verse (verse 5). Bhaskara spotted that two very different stories share one equation, which is the heart of mathematical modelling. The triangle is 12, 16, 20: the 3, 4, 5 triangle scaled by 4.
